Definition: from G2095 and G32; to announce good news ("evangelize") especially the gospel:--declare, bring (declare, show) glad (good) tidings, preach (the gospel).
BiblicalUsage: Euangelízō means to announce good news — to evangelize, to preach the gospel. The angel brings good tidings of great joy to the shepherds; Philip preaches Christ to the Ethiopian; Paul says woe is unto him if he preaches not the gospel. It is the verb of the whole mission.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe euangelízō is the church's first job: to announce the good news, not to keep it. I hold that Paul's 'woe is me' is the measure — if I am not telling it, something is wrong.
RelatedEvents: The Birth of Jesus; The Resurrection
